_about: Cause-and-effect points for each move: what was said or done, and what it did to prices (numbers from the site's price data over the move's days). Written from that week's headlines. Key as in move_summaries.json.
ai|2026-10-12: Broadcom's and Intel's CEOs warned that the money funding AI data centres may not keep flowing → investors questioned how long chip orders can grow → Broadcom −9%, Intel −14%, and the chip-equipment makers that depend on new factories fell hardest: Applied Materials −19%, Lam Research −17%.
Microsoft said it is developing its own AI chip → a big customer needing fewer Nvidia chips → Nvidia −7%, while Microsoft itself barely moved (−1%).
Chinese memory maker CXMT showed progress on a new design and Huawei closed the gap with Nvidia in China → memory chip prices could fall → Micron −15%.
Oil near $110 a barrel → higher costs and inflation fears → investors sold the most expensive stocks first; the Nasdaq 100 fell 5.5% vs 2.0% for the S&P 500, while energy stocks rose 4.9%.
Investors moved money into safety → long-term Treasury bonds rose 2.7%.
ai|2026-09-16: The Federal Reserve's meeting calmed rate worries and bond yields fell → long-term Treasury bonds rose 1.3% → expensive growth stocks became more attractive again.
Investors decided earlier fears about AI spending were overdone → buyers returned to the chipmakers that had fallen most: Intel +28%, AMD +24%, Arm +38%.
Money came out of energy (energy stocks −5.7%) and went back into tech, pushing the Nasdaq to a record high (+6.2% for the Nasdaq 100).
ai|2026-07-29: Strong demand for memory chips → Micron +9%, and South Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung had their best days on record.
Earnings beat expectations → Palantir +32%, Microsoft +25%, Oracle +21%.
Analysts (Goldman Sachs among them) said the July sell-off had gone too far → dip-buying across the basket: Marvell +25%, Lam Research +18%.
ai|2026-07-23: Investors worried Big Tech's AI spending was too high just before those companies reported earnings → they sold the suppliers first: Micron −23%, Marvell −23%, AMD −22%, Applied Materials −21%.
The Iran war pushed oil up, which lifted bond yields → higher rates hurt expensive tech most → Nasdaq 100 −6.2% vs S&P 500 −2.4%.
Even strong earnings didn't help: the semiconductor index fell 6% in one day despite good results, a sign investors were selling on valuation, not on bad numbers.
ai|2026-06-04: Broadcom's results disappointed the market → Broadcom −22% and the chips tied to it fell: Arm −25%, Super Micro −38%, Marvell −16%.
Odds of a Fed rate hike rose → the Nasdaq and S&P 500 had their worst day of the year (S&P 500 −3.8% over the move).
Gold fell 8.2% at the same time, so investors were selling winners across markets, not only tech.
ai|2026-05-19: Fear of missing out before Nvidia's results drove a buying frenzy in smaller chip names → Arm +87%, Marvell +72%, Super Micro +63%, Micron +56%.
Nvidia itself was flat (0%), so the rally was speculation on suppliers rather than on Nvidia's own business.
Bond yields fell (long-term Treasuries +2.9%), which made pricey growth stocks easier to justify; short sellers and some experts warned prices had moved too fast.
ai|2026-04-30: Big Tech companies said they would keep spending heavily on AI data centres → their suppliers rose: Micron +29%, AMD +25%, Super Micro +32%.
AMD and Qualcomm reported strong results → AMD +25%, Intel +19%.
Meta fell 8% at the same time, because investors worried about how much it is spending on AI.
ai|2026-04-08: President Trump announced a ceasefire with Iran → oil fell and energy stocks dropped 7.0% → fears about inflation and the economy eased → tech led the rebound (Nasdaq 100 +6.8%).
TSMC reported strong monthly sales → proof AI chip demand was still growing → Micron +23%, Marvell +22%, Lam Research +21%.
Palantir was the exception (−10%), on worries about its high valuation.
ai|2025-09-04: Oracle forecast its AI-driven cloud revenue would jump to $144 billion → Oracle +47% over the move, including a 36% jump on 10 Sep, its best day since 1992.
Broadcom revealed a $10 billion custom AI chip order → Broadcom +22%.
Investors took both as proof AI spending was still rising → Micron +18%, Arm +17%, TSMC +13%; long-term Treasury bonds also rose 3.7% as yields fell.
ai|2025-05-07: The Trump administration moved to scrap Biden-era limits on exporting AI chips → more countries can buy US chips → Nvidia +19%, AMD +19%.
Nvidia and AMD signed large chip deals with Saudi Arabia → new buyers outside China → Super Micro +37%, Palantir +20%.
The US–China trade truce lifted the whole market (S&P 500 +5.2%); gold fell 7.1% as fear eased.
ai|2025-04-22: The trade war eased and President Trump softened his tone on China and on the Fed → the whole market rebounded (S&P 500 +7.2%).
Wall Street (Morgan Stanley among them) called fears of an AI slowdown overdone → Palantir +24%, Super Micro +24%, Micron +20%, Nvidia +15%.
ai|2025-04-07: President Trump paused most of his new tariffs for 90 days → the biggest one-day rally in years (S&P 500 +8.6%, Nasdaq 100 +10.3%).
Reports said he would hold off on curbing Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China → Nvidia +21%, Broadcom +27%.
Long-term Treasury bonds fell 4.3% at the same time: bond investors were still nervous even as stocks bounced.
ai|2025-03-31: President Trump announced sweeping 'Liberation Day' tariffs on almost every country → fears of a global recession → the S&P 500 fell 9.1%.
Chipmakers rely on factories in Asia and global sales → Micron −27%, Marvell −20%, Arm −19%, Nvidia −14%, even though chips were partly exempt from the tariffs.
Investors fled to safety: long-term Treasury bonds +3.4%, high-yield bonds −2.1%, energy stocks −14.8% on recession fears.
ai|2025-02-21: Reports of possible new US export controls on chips → fewer sales to China → Nvidia −14%, AMD −13%, Broadcom −13%.
Lingering doubts after DeepSeek about how much AI computing is really needed → Super Micro −28%, Palantir −20%.
Weak US economic data pushed investors into bonds (long-term Treasuries +3.1%); the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.9%.
ai|2025-01-15: President Trump announced the $500 billion 'Stargate' AI data-centre project with OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank → Oracle +18%, Arm +28% (SoftBank owns most of Arm).
Strong bank earnings and milder inflation data lifted the whole market (S&P 500 +4.2%), adding to the AI rally: Nvidia +12%, Palantir +17%.
defense|2026-08-17: L3Harris's CEO stepped down after a conduct review → L3Harris −10%.
Lockheed Martin dropped (−9%) and drone maker AeroVironment fell 24% as investors took profits after a strong run.
Investors moved into gold (+6.6%) and Treasury bonds (+1.7%) rather than defense stocks.
defense|2026-07-31: Strong quarterly results from defense tech and services firms → Leidos +24%, Booz Allen +14%, AeroVironment +29%, Kratos rallied on an upgrade.
SpaceX and contractors passed a 'Golden Dome' missile-defense test → hopes of big new contracts.
Palantir, which sells to the military, rose 43% after crushing earnings.
defense|2026-07-20: Lockheed Martin reported a record order backlog → Lockheed +14%, its biggest one-day jump in nearly 25 years.
That lifted the rest of the sector even as the Nasdaq fell 2.9%: RTX +13%, Booz Allen +12%, Huntington Ingalls +11%.
defense|2026-06-26: AeroVironment posted a record quarter → AeroVironment +40%.
NATO members prepared to commit to more defense spending at their summit, and the UK added $20 billion → Northrop +10%, General Dynamics +9%, Leidos +9%.
defense|2026-06-12: Talk of an Iran peace deal → less expected demand for weapons → the sector fell into a bear market.
Germany reportedly scrapped warship orders → European defense fell (Rheinmetall −18% in a day) and US names followed: Booz Allen −23%, AeroVironment −26%, Leidos −18%.
Energy stocks also fell 4.6% on the peace talk, while the S&P 500 was flat (−0.2%): this was a war-trade unwind, not a market sell-off.
defense|2026-04-16: Worries about the Pentagon's budget request before Defense Secretary Hegseth's testimony → the big prime contractors fell: Lockheed −16%, Northrop −15%, RTX −13%.
Investors also reassessed who really profits from the Iran war; defense fell even as the S&P 500 rose 2.2%.
defense|2026-02-12: Investors looked for companies that benefit from conflict and bigger military budgets while the market slipped (S&P 500 −1.1%) → Huntington Ingalls +13%, Northrop +9%, AeroVironment +16%.
defense|2025-12-30: President Trump floated a $1.5 trillion defense budget → Lockheed +18%, Huntington Ingalls +21%, L3Harris +15%.
The US struck Venezuela, raising war risks → drone maker AeroVironment +52%; oil and energy stocks also rose (+6.7%) and gold +6.2%.
defense|2025-09-30: More military spending promised abroad (Japan's new leader, Canada, Europe) → AeroVironment +27%, Leidos +7%.
defense|2025-06-25: NATO members agreed to raise defense spending toward 5% of GDP → steady gains for the big contractors (+2–4%).
defense|2025-04-07: The 90-day tariff pause lifted the whole market (S&P 500 +6.7%).
Europe's push to spend more on defense, partly from a loss of trust in the US, added to it → Huntington Ingalls +19%, AeroVironment +28%, Palantir +25%.
banks|2025-05-07: The US and China agreed a trade truce → recession fears faded → investment banks that earn from deals rose most: Goldman +11%, Morgan Stanley +11%, Bank of America +10%.
banks|2025-04-22: The trade war eased and hedge funds returned to bank shares (Goldman reported) → Citi +9%, Goldman +9%, Wells Fargo +8%.
banks|2025-04-09: President Trump paused most tariffs for 90 days → the market jumped 10.5% in a day; banks rose with it (Goldman +12%, Morgan Stanley +11%).
A week later Citigroup's results showed the market chaos had lifted its trading revenue.
banks|2025-03-28: The 'Liberation Day' tariffs raised the risk of a recession → fewer loans and more defaults → Bank of America −19%, Citi −19%.
Mergers and stock sales froze → less fee income for investment banks → Goldman −16%, Morgan Stanley −16%.
Credit markets showed stress: high-yield bonds −2.3%.
banks|2025-03-03: Tariff threats and weak economic data raised recession fears → banks fell more than twice as much as the market (−12.6% vs −5.7%): Citi −16%, Morgan Stanley −16%, Goldman −15%.
banks|2025-01-13: The big banks reported strong fourth-quarter profits → Citi +14%, Goldman +13%, Wells Fargo +11%.
A milder inflation report raised hopes of rate cuts → the market rose 3.9% and bonds rallied (+2.9%).
oil|2026-08-06: The Iran ceasefire ended and a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping route, stayed out of reach → oil prices rose about 5% in a day.
Refiners earned record profits on high fuel prices → Marathon Petroleum +19%, Phillips 66 +15%; producers rose less (Exxon +6%, Chevron +7%).
Higher oil pushed bond yields up (Treasuries −1.2%), which weighed on other stocks.
oil|2026-07-07: Renewed US–Iran fighting lifted oil prices; Goldman said oil could pass $120 if Hormuz shipping stays disrupted → Occidental +12%, Phillips 66 +12%, Chevron +8%.
Oil stocks rose while the S&P 500 fell 0.3%.
oil|2026-03-23: Oil prices swung on mixed signals about Iran peace talks, but stayed high → oilfield service firms jumped: Schlumberger +15%, Halliburton +11%.
The rest of the market fell (S&P 500 −2.2%), so oil stocks were one of the few places to hide.
oil|2025-12-29: The US struck Venezuela and President Trump promised US companies would revive its oil industry → oilfield service firms that would do the work rose most: Schlumberger +16%, Halliburton +14%; Chevron, already in Venezuela, +9%.
oil|2025-05-07: The US–China trade truce raised hopes for fuel demand → refiners rose most: Phillips 66 +19%, Marathon Petroleum +13%, Occidental +13%.
oil|2025-03-28: The 'Liberation Day' tariffs raised fears of a global recession → less demand for fuel.
At the same time OPEC+ surprised by pumping more oil → oil had its steepest fall in 3 years.
Result: Occidental −27%, Phillips 66 −26%, Schlumberger −24%, Exxon −15%; energy stocks overall −17.7%.
health|2026-10-09: Investors pulled money out of AI and chip stocks (Nasdaq 100 −4.0%) and moved it into steadier sectors → UnitedHealth +13%, Lilly +10%, Pfizer +8%.
Moderna rose 23% on its own news.
health|2026-08-17: Moderna's melanoma vaccine succeeded in a trial → Moderna +119%.
With chip stocks in a bear market, investors bought big drugmakers as a safer place: Merck +11%, Lilly +6%, AbbVie +6%.
health|2026-06-22: Investors moved out of tech into healthcare as a safe haven → AbbVie +17%, Merck +14%, J&J +13%, Lilly +12%, several to record highs.
health|2025-11-06: Investors rotated out of expensive tech (Nasdaq 100 −0.4%) into healthcare → Lilly +10%, Merck +8%, AbbVie +8%.
Hopes for an end to the government shutdown helped too.
health|2025-09-25: Pfizer struck a deal with President Trump on US drug prices → a big worry for drugmakers was removed → Pfizer +14%, Lilly +13%, Merck +12%, Thermo Fisher +16%.
health|2025-08-11: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway revealed a new stake in UnitedHealth → UnitedHealth +21%, its best day since 2020.
health|2025-05-05: President Trump ordered lower US drug prices → drugmakers fell: Lilly −13%, Merck −12%, AbbVie −11%.
UnitedHealth's CEO left abruptly, the company pulled its forecast and reports of a Medicare fraud probe followed → UnitedHealth −23%.
This happened while the market rose 3.7%: it was healthcare's own bad news.
health|2025-03-31: President Trump threatened tariffs on imported medicines → drugmakers fell: AbbVie −14%, Pfizer −13%, Merck −12%.
A top FDA vaccine official resigned in protest at RFK Jr. → Moderna −21%.
Health insurers went the other way after a Medicare pay rise (UnitedHealth +7%).
health|2025-01-21: Excitement over weight-loss drugs continued → Lilly +11%; Moderna +22%.
drop|2026-10-22: Meta's results showed even bigger AI spending plans → Meta −8%, and investors questioned AI returns again → Nvidia −5%, Broadcom −5%, Amazon −5%.
Oil prices surged → energy stocks +1.7% while the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.9%.
Investors moved into safe Treasury bonds (+1.4%); hedge funds had their widest one-day losses since Covid.
drop|2026-10-12: Broadcom's and Intel's CEOs warned about how AI spending is funded → Broadcom −9%, Oracle −9%, Nvidia −7%.
Chinese chipmakers showed progress → memory chip stocks fell.
Oil near $110 → energy stocks +4.9% and Exxon +6%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 5.5% against 2.0% for the S&P 500.
drop|2026-07-13: The war with Iran escalated → oil jumped → Exxon +13%, energy stocks +6.5%.
The Fed paused instead of cutting rates → long-term Treasury bonds fell 1.9% (yields rose) → expensive growth stocks fell most: Tesla −27%, Oracle −16%, Meta −12%, Nvidia −10%.
Apple rose 7%: investors treated it as a safer tech stock. The Nasdaq 100 fell 8.8%, far more than the S&P 500's 3.4%.
drop|2026-06-23: Fears of a memory-chip shortage and doubts about AI → Oracle −15%, Nvidia −8%, Broadcom −7%; Micron and Sandisk were among the biggest losers.
South Korea's chip-heavy market plunged about 10% → the sell-off went global.
drop|2026-06-01: Another wave of AI-stock selling → Broadcom −17%, Microsoft −12%, Amazon −12%, Meta −10%.
South Korea's market crashed and Iran negotiations added uncertainty.
Gold fell 10.2% at the same time: investors sold winners everywhere. Banks (JPMorgan +3%) and oil (Exxon +4%) rose.
drop|2026-03-26: The Iran war widened → oil rose (Exxon +5%) and investors dumped high-flying chip stocks → Meta −10%, Nvidia −8%, Broadcom −8%, Tesla −8%.
The Nasdaq fell into a correction, 10% below its record.
drop|2026-03-12: The Iran war sent oil to $100 a barrel → energy stocks +0.9% while most others fell.
Worries about private credit funds (investors pulling money out) → banks fell (JPMorgan −2%) and high-yield bonds −0.6%.
drop|2026-02-12: New AI tools raised fears that AI will replace whole industries → software, real-estate, trucking and memory stocks fell.
Gold, silver and crypto crashed at the same time (gold −3.5%) → investors were selling across markets; Apple −5%.
drop|2026-01-29: Big Tech announced even bigger AI budgets → investors worried about the payoff → Microsoft −18%, Oracle −21%, Nvidia −10%.
New AI models (Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 among them) raised fears they will replace software companies → US software stocks lost about $1 trillion in a week.
Apple (+8%), JPMorgan (+3%) and Exxon (+6%) rose: money moved out of AI-exposed stocks. Gold fell 10.7%.
drop|2026-01-20: President Trump threatened tariffs on European countries over Greenland → Wall Street's biggest daily drop in three months (S&P 500 −2.0%), led by tech: Oracle −6%, Broadcom −5%, Nvidia −4%.
Bond prices fell too (Treasuries −1.3%) and gold rose 3.8% as a safe haven.
Stocks rebounded once Trump announced a Greenland framework.
drop|2025-12-11: Oracle reported problems funding its AI data centres → Oracle −20%.
Broadcom warned its profit margins would shrink → Broadcom −21%, and investors worried AI spending wasn't paying off → Nvidia −7%, Alphabet −7%.
The Fed cut rates but signalled fewer cuts ahead.
drop|2025-11-13: Investors scaled back hopes for a December Fed rate cut → the market fell 4.5%.
Nvidia reported very strong results but its stock still fell (−7%): investors were already worried about an AI bubble.
A crypto sell-off spread to stocks; Amazon −11%, JPMorgan −7%.
drop|2025-11-04: The CEOs of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley warned of a 10–20% market correction → highly valued AI stocks fell: Nvidia −4%, Palantir tumbled; SoftBank −10% in Tokyo.
drop|2025-10-10: President Trump threatened big new tariffs on China after China tightened rare-earth export rules → about $2 trillion was wiped off US stocks in a day.
Chipmakers with China exposure fell most (Broadcom −6%, Nvidia −5%); investors moved into Treasury bonds (+1.6%).
drop|2025-08-01: President Trump unveiled new tariffs on dozens of countries → stocks fell.
The monthly jobs report was weak and earlier months were revised down → recession fears; bonds rose (+1.4%).
Amazon fell 8% after its cloud results raised questions about its AI plans.
drop|2025-05-21: The US lost its last top credit rating and Trump's tax bill raised worries about government debt → a weak Treasury auction → long-term bond prices fell 1.7% (yields rose).
Higher yields hurt stocks broadly: real estate, healthcare and banks fell most.
drop|2025-03-28: President Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs hit almost every country → fears of a global trade war and recession → the S&P 500 fell 12.5% in seven trading days.
Companies that make goods abroad fell most: Apple −23%, Tesla −19%, Amazon −15%.
Oil also crashed on recession fears and an OPEC+ output increase → Exxon −15%, energy stocks −17.7%.
Credit markets showed stress: high-yield bonds −3.6%.
drop|2025-02-21: Tariff threats against Canada, Mexico and China hit business and consumer confidence → the S&P 500 fell into a correction (−9.7%).
Weak economic data raised fears of a slowdown → investors moved into Treasury bonds (+2.7%).
The most expensive stocks fell most: Tesla −32%, Nvidia −17%, Oracle −16%.
drop|2025-01-27: China's DeepSeek released an AI model that matched US models at a fraction of the cost → investors questioned whether so many expensive AI chips are needed.
Nvidia −17% in one day (about $590 billion, the biggest one-day loss in history), Broadcom −17%, Oracle −14%.
Apple (+3%) and Meta (+2%) rose: cheaper AI helps companies that use it.
drop|2025-01-10: A stronger-than-expected jobs report → fewer rate cuts expected → the 10-year Treasury yield neared 5% (long-term bonds −0.7%) → stocks fell 1.5%.
now|ai|2026-10-23: Chip stocks fell for 8 straight days up to 16 Oct, matching their worst streak since 2008 (about $2 trillion erased); the basket is down 15.2% over the past month.
AI stocks bounced on 19 Oct (CoreWeave got a Goldman upgrade), then slid after Tesla's and Meta's results on 22 Oct revived spending worries.
Over the week the chip-equipment makers fell most: Lam Research −12.8%, KLA −12.2%, Applied Materials −7.8%, Arm −7.7%.
now|defense|2026-10-23: Defense companies reported third-quarter results (Northrop's were called 'good enough'; Lockheed raised its guidance) → Lockheed +9.4%, Leidos +9.0%, Northrop +6.1% this week.
Goldman Sachs told investors worried about the AI rally failing to buy defensive stocks; defense rose 3.8% while the S&P 500 fell 0.4%.
On 19 Oct defense dipped on bets that Democrats sweep the elections and spend less on the military.
now|banks|2026-10-23: The big US banks had their longest losing streak since 2008 despite decent earnings → Citi −2.9%, JPMorgan −2.4% this week; −3.6% for the basket over the month.
Regional banks went the other way: KRE +3.8%, PNC +3.3%.
now|oil|2026-10-23: Middle East and Russia–Ukraine tensions kept oil near $110 → the basket is up 11.7% over the past month.
US emergency oil reserves fell to their lowest since 1982 → less cushion if supply is cut.
On 19 Oct oil dipped when President Trump put Russia sanctions on hold; this week oilfield services still led: Schlumberger +7.2%, Halliburton +4.2%, Chevron +3.7%.
now|health|2026-10-23: Investors kept moving money out of AI and chip stocks into healthcare → healthcare led the market on 20 Oct.
UnitedHealth +4.2% and J&J +3.2% this week; the basket is up 4.2% over the past month.
today|all|2026-10-23: Meta's and Tesla's results on 22 Oct revived worries about how much is being spent on AI → AI-linked stocks stayed under pressure: Bloom Energy, which supplies power to data centres, −11.2%.
Oil prices jumped again → oil stocks +2.9% while the S&P 500 fell 0.5%.
Telecoms fell sharply: AT&T −8.0%, T-Mobile −7.7% (the news we have doesn't yet say why).
Cybersecurity went the other way: CrowdStrike +8.3%.
now|all|2026-10-23: Fears about AI spending spread from chipmakers to the companies that build AI data centres and their power: Howmet −15.9%, Quanta Services −13.5%, Lam Research −12.8% this week.
Rising financing costs were reported to threaten the AI spending boom, and investor Michael Burry warned of a 2000-style crash → investors cut risk before Big Tech's earnings.
The S&P 500 ended the week only −0.4% because money moved into defensive sectors: healthcare +0.9%, defense +3.8%, oil +2.0%.
today|ai|2026-10-23: After an 8-day losing streak, buyers returned to the biggest losers → Micron +2.5%, Marvell +2.3%, AMD +1.7%.
The rebound was small: AI stocks had slid on 22 Oct as spending worries festered after Tesla's and Meta's earnings, and Super Micro still fell 2.3%.
today|defense|2026-10-23: Lockheed Martin raised its guidance → Lockheed +2.4% today, on top of +9.4% this week.
Drone maker AeroVironment +4.7%; RTX −1.9% and Huntington Ingalls −1.7% went the other way.
today|banks|2026-10-23: A day after European banks tumbled as oil climbed (22 Oct), US investment banks fell most: Morgan Stanley −2.4%, Goldman Sachs −1.8%, Citi −1.5%, JPMorgan −1.5%.
today|oil|2026-10-23: US crude stockpiles fell more than expected (reported 21 Oct) and oil prices jumped again on 22 Oct → oil stocks +2.9% today while the S&P 500 fell 0.5%.
Oilfield service companies, which gain when drilling picks up, led: Schlumberger +7.1%, Halliburton +5.2%; producers ConocoPhillips +3.6%, EOG +3.2%.
today|health|2026-10-23: After a strong month (+4.2%), the biggest names slipped: Lilly −2.5%, UnitedHealth −1.6%, J&J −1.4%, Merck −1.3%.
